# Visual Algos

A **desktop app** that turns a computer-science topic into a
**3Blue1Brown-style [Manim](https://www.manim.community/) video** — generated by
AI and **rendered locally on your machine**. Type a topic, Gemini writes the
Manim scene, and the app renders a real MP4 into your library.

**Install-and-go:** the app ships its own Python + Manim + ffmpeg runtime, so
there are **no commands to run and nothing to install** beyond the app itself.
The only setup is pasting a free Gemini API key. Nothing leaves your machine
except the topic text you send to Gemini.

## Install (for users)

1. Download the installer for your OS from the project's **Releases** page:
   - **macOS** — `.dmg`
   - **Windows** — `.exe` installer
   - **Linux** — `.AppImage`
2. Open it and launch **Visual Algos**.
3. In **Settings**, paste a free **Gemini API key**
   ([get one here](https://aistudio.google.com/apikey)) — it's stored locally.
4. Go to **New**, type a topic, and generate.

That's it. macOS and Windows builds are fully self-contained. Linux relies on
`libpango`/`libcairo` being present, which they almost always are on a desktop
that can run the app.

> The installer is on the larger side (~250–350 MB) because it bundles a
> complete Manim rendering runtime. Builds are currently **unsigned**, so on
> first launch macOS Gatekeeper / Windows SmartScreen may ask you to confirm.
>
> Mathematical formulas via LaTeX (`MathTex`) aren't bundled (LaTeX is
> gigabytes); the app animates with on-screen `Text` instead.

## Features

- **Code-follows-line videos** — the algorithm's source stays on screen and the
  executing line is highlighted in sync with the data animation.
- **Local rendering** — Manim runs on your machine via the bundled runtime; no
  servers, no per-render fees.
- **Model picker** — choose any Gemini model (dropdown of common ones, or enter
  a custom id) in Settings.
- **AI narration (optional)** — add an ElevenLabs key to generate a voiceover
  that's muxed into the video.
- **Auto-repair** — if generated code fails to render, the traceback is fed back
  to Gemini and the scene is fixed and re-rendered (up to 2 tries).
- **Regenerate** — retry any video (fresh take or after an error) from its page.
- **Cost estimate** — an approximate per-video API cost is shown before you
  generate.
- **Auto-update** — installed apps update themselves from GitHub Releases.

## How it works

1. You add a **Gemini API key** in Settings (stored locally in `userData`).
2. On **New**, you enter a topic. The main process asks **Gemini** for a
   self-contained Manim scene (plus a narration script) and runs a **static
   safety scan** on the code.
3. It writes the scene to a temp dir and runs the **bundled Manim** (bundled
   Python + bundled ffmpeg) to render an MP4. If the render fails, the code +
   traceback go back to Gemini for a fix and it retries.
4. If narration is on, the script is synthesized with **ElevenLabs** and muxed
   onto the video with ffmpeg.
5. The library and detail pages update **live** over IPC as the job moves
   through *Writing scene → Rendering → Ready*, then play the video.

Everything is stored locally under Electron's per-user `userData` dir:
`library.json` (metadata), `videos/<id>.mp4` (renders), `settings.json`.

## Build from source (for developers)

```bash
npm install
npm run setup:python   # downloads a standalone Python + installs Manim into resources/pyruntime
npm run dev            # launches the app with hot reload
```

On **Linux**, `manimpango` compiles from source (no Linux wheel exists), so
install its build deps once before `setup:python`:

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y libpango1.0-dev libcairo2-dev pkg-config build-essential
```

macOS and Windows use prebuilt wheels — no system deps needed.

### Package installers locally

```bash
npm run package        # runs setup:python, builds, then electron-builder → dist/
```

Produces a `.dmg`/`.zip` (macOS), `.exe` (Windows), or `.AppImage` (Linux) for
the OS you run it on. Native runtimes are platform-specific, so build each OS's
installer on that OS.

### Produce installers for everyone (CI)

`.github/workflows/build.yml` builds installers on macOS, Windows, and Linux
runners with the runtime bundled in. **Push a tag** (e.g. `v0.1.0`) and the
installers are attached to a GitHub Release automatically — no local commands,
no per-user setup:

```bash
git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0
```

You can also trigger it manually from the Actions tab to get build artifacts
without cutting a release.

## Updates (auto-update)

Installed apps update themselves via
[`electron-updater`](https://www.electron.build/auto-update). On a **tag** push,
CI runs `electron-builder --publish always`, which uploads the installers **plus
update metadata** (`latest*.yml` + blockmaps) to the GitHub Release for that
version. Running apps check that feed on launch, download a newer version in the
background, and show a "Restart to update" banner. On Windows the download is
block-level differential, so if only the app code changed (not the ~440 MB
Python runtime) the delta is small.

To ship an update:

```bash
# bump "version" in package.json (e.g. 0.1.1), commit, then:
git tag v0.1.1 && git push origin v0.1.1
```

(The tag must match the `version` in `package.json`.) Auto-update needs
published releases; unsigned builds still update, but users see the usual OS
"unidentified developer" prompts until you add code signing.

## The bundled runtime

`scripts/setup-python-runtime.mjs` builds `resources/pyruntime`:

- Downloads a relocatable CPython from
  [`python-build-standalone`](https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone).
- `pip install manim imageio-ffmpeg` into it (imageio-ffmpeg provides a static
  ffmpeg — no system ffmpeg needed).
- Trims caches/tests to keep the size down.

`electron-builder` packs it as an `extraResource`, so at runtime it lives at
`process.resourcesPath/pyruntime`. The app prefers this bundled interpreter; if
it's absent (a bare source checkout), it falls back to a managed venv or your
system Python, and Settings offers a one-click "Install Manim for me".

## Project layout

```
src/
  shared/types.ts        Shared types + IPC channel names (main ⇄ renderer)
  main/                  Electron main process
    index.ts             App lifecycle, window, vizmedia:// protocol
    ipc.ts               IPC handlers + change broadcast
    service.ts           create → Gemini → render pipeline
    gemini.ts            Gemini call
    manim.ts             Local Manim render via child_process (+ ffmpeg wiring)
    manimPrompt.ts       Prompt, response schema, code safety scan
    env.ts               Bundled/managed/system python + ffmpeg resolution
    store.ts             Local JSON store (settings + library)
    paths.ts             userData paths
  preload/index.ts       contextBridge → window.api
  renderer/              React UI (Vite + Tailwind + React Router)
    src/pages/           Library, New, Detail, Settings
scripts/
  setup-python-runtime.mjs   Builds the bundled Python + Manim runtime
.github/workflows/build.yml  Cross-platform installer builds
```

## Security notes

- **Context isolation is on**; the renderer has no Node access and talks to the
  main process only through the typed `window.api` bridge.
- The generated Python is **arbitrary code executed by Manim**. Mitigations:
  a **static denylist** rejects `os`, `subprocess`, `open`, `eval`, `exec`,
  sockets, etc. before rendering; it runs under your own user account and only
  writes to a temp dir and the app's videos folder. Stronger per-render
  sandboxing (container/gVisor) is a good follow-up.
- Your Gemini API key is stored in plain JSON under `userData` — typical for a
  local tool; a future version could use the OS keychain.
